blocks.raw: # aiRA Coder
blocks.text: aiRA Coder

blocks.raw: Know what aiRA coder is and it's capabilities
blocks.text: Know what aiRA coder is and it's capabilities

blocks.raw: Connect+ includes a built-in AI assistant called aiRA Coder. It is integrated directly into the dataflow canvas and lets you build, understand, and manage dataflows through plain-language conversation. Instead of assembling every block manually or writing transformation scripts from scratch, you describe what you want and aiRA Coder generates the result.
blocks.text: Connect+ includes a built-in AI assistant called aiRA Coder. It is integrated directly into the dataflow canvas and lets you build, understand, and manage dataflows through plain-language conversation. Instead of assembling every block manually or writing transformation scripts from scratch, you describe what you want and aiRA Coder generates the result.

blocks.raw: aiRA Coder is available by default in the Connect+ UI. No separate setup is required. You access it by clicking the  icon in the bottom-right corner of any dataflow canvas.
blocks.text: aiRA Coder is available by default in the Connect+ UI. No separate setup is required. You access it by clicking the  icon in the bottom-right corner of any dataflow canvas.

blocks.raw: aiRA Coder is particularly useful for bridging the gap between technical and non-technical users. Standard integration patterns can be generated without knowing which blocks to select or what scripts to write. For experienced developers, it speeds up repetitive configuration tasks and makes it easier to understand flows built by others.

blocks.raw: ## How aiRA Coder works
blocks.text: How aiRA Coder works

blocks.raw: Every prompt you enter goes through a five-step process before any output is shown on the canvas.
blocks.text: Every prompt you enter goes through a five-step process before any output is shown on the canvas.

blocks.raw:
1. **Prompt enrichment**: The system enhances your input using Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Relevant context and examples are added to your prompt before it reaches the language model.

2. **Intent interpretation**: The language model analyses the enriched prompt and identifies what you are trying to accomplish.

3. **Dataflow generation**: Based on the interpreted intent, the system generates a draft configuration. This includes the required blocks, connections, and any transformation scripts.

4. **Validation**: A system-level validator checks the generated output for missing or misconfigured blocks, empty nodes, and syntax issues in script blocks.

5. **Preview and explanation**: The validated draft appears on the canvas alongside a step-by-step explanation of each block. You can accept the output, request changes with a new prompt, or discard and regenerate.

blocks.raw: ## Capabilities
blocks.text: Capabilities

blocks.raw: aiRA Coder supports five distinct capabilities. Each is described below with guidance on when to use it and example prompts.

blocks.raw: ### Create a dataflow
blocks.text: Create a dataflow

blocks.raw: You can describe a dataflow requirement in plain language and aiRA Coder generates the full block sequence, including transformation scripts where needed.
blocks.text: You can describe a dataflow requirement in plain language and aiRA Coder generates the full block sequence, including transformation scripts where needed.

blocks.raw: This is the fastest way to start a new dataflow when a matching global template does not exist or when your use case has specific requirements that a template does not cover.
blocks.text: This is the fastest way to start a new dataflow when a matching global template does not exist or when your use case has specific requirements that a template does not cover.

blocks.raw: **When to use this**: When building a new dataflow from scratch and you have a clear description of the source, transformation, and destination.
blocks.text: When to use this: When building a new dataflow from scratch and you have a clear description of the source, transformation, and destination.

blocks.raw: **How to use it**:
blocks.text: How to use it:

blocks.raw:
1. Create a new dataflow and open the canvas. 2. Click the chat icon in the bottom-right corner to open aiRA Coder. 3. Select **Create dataflow**.
A list of templates appears. 4. Select a template or enter a prompt to create a dataflow based on your requirements. 5. Click the **Send** icon to submit the prompt.
aiRA returns a proposed dataflow with a step-by-step explanation and a preview. 6. Review the changes. 7. Click **Close Preview** to close the preview without making any changes. 8. To accept or reject changes, open the **aiRA Coder** modal by clicking **aiRA Coder**. In the modal, you can: * **Accept Preview** – Save and apply the AI-generated changes. * **Reject Preview** – Discard the AI-generated changes.

blocks.raw: ### Modify a dataflow
blocks.text: Modify a dataflow

blocks.raw: You can use aiRA Coder to update an existing dataflow in Draft state. Instead of editing block configurations manually, you describe the change you want, and aiRA Coder applies it.
blocks.text: You can use aiRA Coder to update an existing dataflow in Draft state. Instead of editing block configurations manually, you describe the change you want, and aiRA Coder applies it.

blocks.raw: Supported modifications include:
blocks.text: Supported modifications include:

blocks.raw:
* Adding or removing blocks
* Changing filter conditions
* Updating JSLT transformation expressions
* Reconfiguring block properties such as API endpoints, group size, and error codes
blocks.text: Adding or removing blocksChanging filter conditionsUpdating JSLT transformation expressionsReconfiguring block properties such as API endpoints, group size, and error codes

blocks.raw: **When to use this**: When you need to make structural or logical changes to a Draft dataflow and want to avoid manual block-level editing.
blocks.text: When to use this: When you need to make structural or logical changes to a Draft dataflow and want to avoid manual block-level editing.

blocks.raw: **How to use it**:
blocks.text: How to use it:

blocks.raw:
1. Open the dataflow in Draft state that needs modification. 2. Click the aiRA Coder icon. 3. Click **Modify Dataflow** or enter a prompt describing the modification.
On clicking **Modify Dataflow** aiRA Coder lists common changes. 4. Click a suggested change or enter a prompt describing your modification click the **Send** icon.
aiRA Coder generates the updated configuration and displays a preview. 5. Review the changes using the Preview icon. 6. After the review, click **Accept** to apply the changes to the canvas or **Reject** to discard the changes. 7. If you selected **Accept**, select **Yes, continue** on the confirmation modal. 8. Click **Save**.

blocks.raw: ### Copy and paste a dataflow
blocks.text: Copy and paste a dataflow

blocks.raw: You can use aiRA Coder to copy a dataflow from one organization and paste it into another, within the same cluster. This removes the need to rebuild common integration patterns from scratch in each organization.
blocks.text: You can use aiRA Coder to copy a dataflow from one organization and paste it into another, within the same cluster. This removes the need to rebuild common integration patterns from scratch in each organization.

blocks.raw: The copy and paste operation requires three sequential prompts: a copy prompt, a view prompt, and a paste prompt. To skip the view step, use the copy and paste options in aiRA Coder. In this case, the view step is integrated with the paste step.

blocks.raw: **Guidelines for copy and paste**:
blocks.text: Guidelines for copy and paste:

blocks.raw:
* Always include a meaningful description in your copy prompt. This is mandatory. If you omit it, aiRA Coder will ask you to provide one.
* Specify a version number in the copy prompt to copy a specific version. If you do not specify a version, aiRA Coder copies the version currently open on the canvas.
* Specify the cluster name in the view prompt. You can only view one cluster at a time.
* The Trigger block and any tags assigned to the dataflow are not copied.
* You can copy and paste only one dataflow at a time.
* The original dataflow remains intact after copying. This feature copies, not moves.

blocks.raw: ## Known limitations
blocks.text: Known limitations

blocks.raw: The following limitations apply to the current version of aiRA Coder. These will be addressed in future releases.
blocks.text: The following limitations apply to the current version of aiRA Coder. These will be addressed in future releases.

blocks.raw:
* Token size limitations may restrict the generation of complex dataflows. If your dataflow is very large, break it into smaller prompts.
* Nesting or calling one dataflow from another is not supported.
* External libraries are not supported.
* aiRA Coder generates a starting configuration. Review all outputs before making a dataflow live.
* Currently, you cannot create a dataflow which uses an API with query parameters.
